:::{#def-differentiable}
#### Differentiable function

A function $f$ is **differentiable at** $x = c$ if the limit (@def-limit)

$$f'(c) \eqdef \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h}$$

exists and is finite.
The number $f'(c)$ is the derivative of $f$ at $c$ (@def-derivative).

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 2.1, p. 100]

:::
